Photo Credit: Gift Eno Ndah/Instagram Nigeria has another reason to celebrate on the international pageant stage. Gift Eno Ndah , Miss Supranational Nigeria 2026, finished as Third Runner-Up at the 17th edition of Miss Supranational, held on 31 July 2026 at the Strzelecki Park Amphitheater in Nowy Sącz, Poland, competing against 66 other contestants from around the world. The Philippines’ Katrina Llegado was crowned Miss Supranational 2026, becoming only the second Filipina to win the title. France’s Eve Gilles finished as First Runner-Up, Brazil’s Lara Marina was named Second Runner-Up, and Nigeria’s Gift Eno Ndah placed Third Runner-Up, with Karolina Gorylova of the Czech Republic completing the Top 5 as Fourth Runner-Up. Gift Eno Ndah wearing an orange embellished gown at Miss Supranational 2026 grand finale where she finished Third Runner-Up. Photo Credit: Gift Eno Ndah/Instagram So who is Gift Eno Ndah? The Akwa Ibom State indigene grew up in Orile Iganmu, Lagos, and is a model, actress, and entrepreneur who champions the empowerment of young women through her Bloom Within project. She was crowned Miss Supranational Nigeria in August 2025 before heading to Poland to represent the country at the international competition in July 2026. Her background shaped her in ways that go beyond the stage. “Growing up in Orile Iganmu gave me a very real understanding of life, community and acceptance,” she has said , and that grounded perspective has been central to how she has carried herself throughout her reign. Official portrait of Gift Eno Ndah crowned as Miss Supranational Nigeria 2026 wearing a gold tiara and official pageant sash. Photo Credit: Gift Eno Ndah/Instagram Her preparation for Poland was intense and deliberate. “It’s been amazing and it’s been very exciting. It’s been so many sleepless nights, and learning and unlearning, but I’m certain that my team and I, we are working together to ensure that we put Nigeria on the map,” she said ahead of the competition. “At this point, it’s beyond just the physical aspect; it is mental, emotional, and purposeful preparation as well.” On what drew her to pageantry in the first place, she has been equally clear. “Beauty pageant has always been a dream. I have seen it transform the lives of other women, turn them into leaders that have made impact in our society today,” she said. Gift Eno Ndah went to Poland with exactly that conviction, and she came home with Nigeria firmly on the Miss Supranational map. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/s.text: Nusrat Osman, a 47-year-old auditor and mother of two, was safe and ‘not too shaken’ after her ordeal, her brother said. Photograph: Family Handout View image in fullscreen Nusrat Osman, a 47-year-old auditor and mother of two, was safe and ‘not too shaken’ after her ordeal, her brother said. Photograph: Family Handout Malawi British woman who was kidnapped in Malawi rescued by police after shootout Four of Nurat Osman’s alleged abductors were killed during rescue after she was taken from outside her home last week Rachel Savage in Johannesburg Fri 18 Sep 2026 07.21 EDT Last modified on Fri 18 Sep 2026 07.35 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A British woman kidnapped in Malawi last week has been rescued by police after a shootout in which four of her alleged abductors were killed. Nusrat Osman was abducted outside her home in the southern city of Blantyre on 11 September at about 12.30pm. Police had offered a reward of 30m Malawi kwacha (£12,950) for information leading to her rescue and the arrest of the perpetrators. Malawian police announced Osman’s rescue late on Thursday in a statement. “There was an exchange of fire between police and kidnappers, who were armed with [an] AK47 rifle and a Girsan Regard MC pistol. In the process, the criminals got shot and were taken to hospital where they succumbed to their injuries.” it read. A police officer, deputy inspector general Mlowoka Noel Kayira, was also shot during the operation. “He is currently receiving medical attention at the hospital and is in a stable condition,” police said. Osman, a 47-year-old auditor and mother of two, was safe and “not too shaken” after her ordeal, her brother Shobi Jiwa told the Sun , expressing his gratitude to Malawi’s police. Jiwa reserved special thanks for Kayira. “He is the hero of our family. He’s the hero of the country,” he said. “He’s the hero of the world, actually, for putting his life at risk and taking a bullet into himself for my sister.” Kidnappings are rare in Malawi, which has experienced a rise in pickpocketing and house burglaries by often armed men in recent years amid unstable, crisis-ridden economic conditions. The landlocked southern African country is one of the world’s poorest nations, with a population of about 22 million and an average annual income of just $672, according to the World Bank . In 2024, a country report by the US state department’s diplomatic security service said: “Kidnappings are not a widespread concern in Malawi, and there have been no recent high-profile incidents involving westerners. “Historically, expatriates have not been significant targets for kidnappings in the country. When kidnappings do occur, they often involve members of the Asian business community rather than foreign travellers or residents.” Osman, who is originally from Leicester, worked for a local audit firm and had lived in Malawi with her husband and children for several years. Before her rescue, her family said they had not had any news of her, including any contact from the kidnappers demanding a ransom. Her husband, Nazil Osman, told the local news outlet Nyasa Times : “I don’t know where she is or how she is. My wife is an auditor, and I have no issues with anyone.” Her brother told the Sun on Tuesday: “My sister has been missing for five days with no trace or call,” adding that the family could not think of a motive for her kidnapping. Police did not say whether information received in response to the offered reward had led to Osman’s rescue, adding that investigations were ongoing and more details would be shared “in due course”. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP Australian politics ‘Are you waiting for me to be attacked?’ Fatima Payman slams PM over office security Albanese promises ‘swift response’ on MP safety as he mulls panic buttons for politicians Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast Josh Butler , Sarah Basford Canales and Josh Taylor Tue 27 Oct 2026 06.12 EDT First published on Tue 27 Oct 2026 01.19 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Anthony Albanese has promised a “swift government response” to safety threats to MPs and floated the provision of duress alarms for electorate offices, saying politicians and their staff have put up with threats for too long. The prime minister’s pledge to the Labor party room came hours after Senator Fatima Payman again slammed her former government colleagues over the lack of staffing given to her office, controversially asking: “Is the prime minister waiting for something, like what happened to Dr Helen Haines, to occur to my office?” MPs across the political divide have spoken forcefully of the need for more protection for their offices after the alleged attack on the Indi MP last week, raising alarm about threats and violence directed to their staff. Politicians are also revealing the scale of abuse, online and offline, directed toward them , including death and rape threats, with Australia’s eSafety commissioner, Julie Inman Grant, telling Senate estimates she and her family had also been subject to online abuse and threats. Labor condemns One Nation cartoons depicting Penny Wong being murdered as Hanson says videos ‘not going anywhere’ Read more In the first Labor party-room meeting since the alleged attack, Albanese gave a long address, saying this week “must be a turning point” for civil discourse and how threats are responded to. He also conceded there needed to be more investment in security and safety for politicians. Albanese said MPs have had to “put up with the threat environment for too long”, that the government “need to do more” and “more can and should be done”. “You’ve all dedicated so much to the safety of others in the workplace. I’m determined to make sure we do everything for your safety and the safety of your staff as well,” he said. Albanese did not give specifics, but promised a “swift government response” on safety, and noted numerous MPs had raised the prospect of receiving duress alarms, or panic buttons, to alert authorities to a safety incident. This was among a “series of options” under consideration. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, also told the meeting that the government was looking at safety at polling booths around election time. Government sources said numerous changes were being considered, with a full response and proposal likely to be revealed in coming days. MPs have raised a wide range of concerns, including greater security and hardening of their electoral offices, better communication with federal police, and resources for security at their private homes such as CCTV and lighting – all options understood to be under consideration. An ongoing review into commonwealth workplaces will also be expedited by Labor, with recommendations specifically about safety and security to be delivered soon. The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, told his MPs in a Coalition party-room meeting of ongoing conversations with the government about personal safety and the importance of getting it right, but did not raise any specific proposals. Payman speaks out Payman, who quit Labor in 2024 to sit on the crossbench, on Monday night lashed out at the prime minister for not responding to a request for additional staff in line with other independent political offices. The prime minister has discretion over the allocation of personal staff, which are typically more senior advisers. All politicians receive electoral office staff, but Payman has zero advisers while 16 other crossbench MPs and senators shared 30 advisers, according to an internal document tabled in the hearing. Graph showing the rise in threats to Australia politicians In a Senate estimates hearing, Payman questioned the minister Don Farrell whether the staff allocation shortfall was due to Albanese having a personal gripe with her, claiming her staff were severely overworked. “If [Albanese] cares so much about the welfare and wellbeing of people who work in this building, then I implore you [Farrell] and the prime minister to please look into the fact that my staff are burning out,” she said. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Politics, really Our political team brings you up to speed on the stories that really matter and what they mean for you after newsletter promotion “Is the prime minister waiting for something, like what happened to Dr Helen Haines , to occur to my office – to me – for him to take our request seriously?” Farrell and other Labor senators in the hearing strongly rejected the insinuation, but Payman refused to withdraw the comments when asked until her staffing request was dealt with. View image in fullscreen Independent Fatima Payman at Senate estimates. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP Payman told Guardian Australia last week there had been a massive increase in the number of death threats and hate comments since 2024 when she defected from Labor. Payman said her office manager had opened mail last year containing human faeces, resulting in a biohazard team having to respond. “We had all these people in hazmat suits come through [the office],” she said. “The trauma that that inflicts on my staff members is horrible. No office or no worker should ever have to deal with that kind of crap.” The eSafety commissioner targeted Inman Grant said in her final appearance before Senate estimates on Tuesday evening that it was a “sensitive and pivotal moment” for parliament in the wake of the alleged attack, and the environment was “dangerously febrile for women in senior government roles”. “When public officials are used for political point scoring, a target goes on our backs and we are subjected to an onslaught of online abuse and threats,” she said. “As many of you know, this has been the normal state of affairs for me and my family for years, yet somehow this is meant to be accepted as part of public service.” Inman Grant did not name any people who have targeted her personally, but her work in the role has seen her labelled as a “censorship commissar” by the world’s richest person, Elon Musk. The US Republican congressman Jim Jordan labelled Inman Grant as a “zealot for global takedowns”. Inman Grant said more needs to be done for the next generation of leaders to feel safe in online spaces or public-facing roles. “Social media is no longer the once envisioned digital town square – it has become more like a gladiatorial arena,” she said. “Meanwhile, platforms continue to roll back abuse and violent speech policies that let some of the most egregious offenders out of digital jail.” Explore more on these topics Australian politics Helen Haines Anthony Albanese Fatima Payman news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Albanese concedes $6m golf club grant in his electorate was not to contain ‘raw sewage’ Labor condemns One Nation cartoons depicting Penny Wong being murdered as Hanson says videos ‘not going anywhere’ The chaos in France is a ‘warning signal’ for Australia’s public spending and rising costs Australians should prepare for online services to go down unexpectedly as threats rise, cyber agency warns Angus Taylor criticised for ‘tone deaf’ response to alleged attack on Helen Haines Helen Haines’s first words after alleged attack revealed as MPs honour her ‘empathy and grace’ Most viewed Most viewed Australia World AU politics Environment Climate crisis Indigenous Australia Immigration Media Business Health Science Tech Podcasts Newsletters
